roots.context: We have learned how feelings change the body and show on the face, and how hard faces can be to read. Now we ask what feelings tell us about ourselves and each other.

deep_truth.truth: In the face test, happy faces were easy to name, but scared and surprised often got mixed up. Both lift the eyebrows and open the eyes wide. So a face gives a few clues, and the watcher guesses the rest. To know how a friend really feels, ask them.
deep_truth.habit: We talk as if we can see a feeling on a face, like reading a word on a page. But a face shows only a few muscle shapes, and the same shapes fit more than one feeling. What we call 'seeing' a feeling is really a guess.
deep_truth.evidence: In the Face Test, scared and surprised were often confused, and in the Real or Polite test some polite smiles fooled the guesser. Scientists found the same: the Fore people of Papua New Guinea and Darwin's visitors also disagreed about some faces.

three.who_am_i: Your feelings are part of your body: your heart, your breath and your face all join in.
three.what_is_life: Living beings feel, and many show it. A dog, a crow and a baby all show feelings without words.
three.what_is_this_world: A world full of other people, each with feelings you can only partly see. Asking is how you reach them.

roots.thread: A feeling begins in one person, yet it does not stay inside them. It moves their face, and a friend's face moves a little in answer. A yawn or a laugh spreads round a room until many people are doing the same thing. In this small way, many separate people share one feeling, and empathy is the name for that sharing.

teachings.teaching: As a crystal shows the colour of what is next to it, the face shows what is strongly felt in the heart.
teachings.link: Thiruvalluvar saw that strong feelings show on the face. The Face Test found that too, and also that some faces are hard to read.

teachings.teaching: A feeling in a play is shown through outward signs, such as the face, the eyes and the body, and the audience comes to taste that feeling themselves.
teachings.link: The outward signs are the same face and body changes this unit studied. The audience tasting the feeling is a kind of empathy.

teachings.teaching: Anyone who suddenly sees a small child about to fall into a well feels alarm and pity at once, before thinking of any reward.
teachings.link: The feeling comes before the thought, just as your heart raced before you knew what the noise was. Caring for others starts as a feeling in the body.

science.text: People often copy each other's faces very slightly without noticing, for example smiling a little when they see a smile.
Whether a few feelings have the same face in every person everywhere is still argued about.
What a feeling is, and how the body and brain together make it, has no agreed answer.

other_view.view: Copying a face or catching a yawn is something human brains are built to do, because it helped our ancestors live in groups. It shows that brains copy each other. It does not show that people share one feeling.

practice.title: Find the feeling in your body
practice.say: Let's sit still and close our eyes. Take three slow breaths. Now notice your body. Is your heart fast or slow? Is your tummy tight or soft? Are your hands warm or cool? Now give the feeling a name, quietly, in your head. Open your eyes. What did you find?
practice.kid: Sit still. Close your eyes. Take three slow breaths. Feel your heart and your tummy. Are they calm or busy? Name the feeling in your head. Open your eyes.

ask: When you guessed a feeling wrong in the Face Test, was the face wrong, or was your guess wrong?
Can you feel something without your body changing at all?
If a friend smiles but feels sad, which one is the truth about her?

playtest: Every experiment, activity, game, project and challenge was walked through as if at home today, in a city flat, with the materials listed. The Face Test needs only paper cards and a notebook, and works with two people. A grown-up makes faces first, because children often find it hard to pose fear. Results vary from family to family, and the parent note says what is common without giving away the answer. The Real or Polite smile test says honestly that many people can fake the eye crinkle, so a score near 5 of 10 is a real result, not a failure. The Catch a Yawn test does the smiling round first, so yawns don't carry over, and suggests swapping the order another day. Children under about five rarely catch yawns, and the note says so. The body map and the Kindness Week need no special materials. The calm corner fits in one bedsheet of space. Timings were checked step by step. The spine fits about 85 minutes.
